KEY MESSAGE 1...
A compact area of low pressure is tracking through the upper
Ohio Valley early this morning, and will exit to the east 
today. A quick-moving batch of rain accompanying this low 
pressure is with us early this morning, but will exit to the 
east-southeast through midday. Aside from some northeast flow 
lake effect showers which are already taking shape off the 
western and central basin early this morning, there will be a 
brief lull in rain across the area around midday. 

This lull won't last long, as a sharp inverted trough axis
behind the departing low drops south-southwest across the area
this afternoon and evening as an embedded shortwave aloft also
crosses the region. This will bring another more widespread
batch of showers to the area this afternoon and evening. It will
be cold and unstable enough for lake enhancement, and some
showers will likely have a convective component...especially
west and southwest of Cleveland. Much of the area is expected 
to see another 0.10-0.25" of rain during the day today (between 
the exiting morning rain and afternoon/evening rain). Locations 
just west and southwest of Cleveland will see more due to lake 
enhancement. Most regional and convective allowing models have a
localized area of 0.50-1.00" of rain where lake enhancement 
is most prominent and the forecast has higher amounts in the 
vicinity of Erie/Huron/Lorain/Richland/Ashland Counties today, 
as the flow direction, increasing instability, and synoptic 
support from the trough suggest that there will be decent lake 
enhancement in that area. 

Temperatures will generally settle into the mid to upper 40s by
sunrise this morning and will rise no more than a couple/few
degrees. If anything, temperatures will backslide this afternoon
as the trough brings rain and increased cold air advection.
Northerly wind gusts will also increase to 20-30 MPH late this
afternoon and evening just behind the passage of the trough. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
We transition to a lake effect rain/snow shower setup to end the
week and start the weekend. There should be a relatively drier 
period with limited lake effect for several hours tonight as we 
see a brief period of subsidence, drier low-level air, and shear
behind this evening's trough. Winds are expected to become 
better aligned out of a north or slightly east of due north 
direction heading into Friday as deeper moisture returns, 
allowing lake effect to re-invigorate. Once lake effect starts 
flaring back up into Friday it will continue in some capacity 
through most of the weekend. Conditions will be most favorable 
for lake effect late tonight through Friday night as the heart 
of the upper trough moves overhead. 500mb temperatures bottom 
out near -30C Friday into Friday night over the region, which 
over lake waters ranging from 12-15C provides strong and deep 
lake-induced instability. The mid-levels will gradually begin to
dry and warm on Saturday, though that probably won't begin to 
significantly curtail the intensity of lake effect until 
Saturday night and Sunday. Lingering minor lake effect may not 
fully end until Monday across far Northeast OH/Northwest PA, as 
that's when the surface high finally builds into the region. 

In terms of where lake effect will go, this will generally be a
shorter fetch event with north-northeast winds tonight into
Friday gradually shifting north-northwest into Friday night and
more northwesterly for the bulk of the weekend. A band of precip
with connection to Lake Huron will be the main feature and
should take shape tonight into Friday well west of Cleveland...
possibly coming onshore as far west as Ottawa County and 
extending towards Tiffin initially. This connection is expected 
to drift east into the Cleveland and Akron metro area later 
Friday into Friday night, and then into the more traditional 
primary snowbelt of far Northeast OH for the weekend. There is 
also a signal on multiple models for convergence along the far 
northeastern lakeshore to focus a more organized band into 
eastern Erie/Crawford Counties in PA Friday into Friday evening 
as well. Outside of these potentially more focused bands 
activity will generally be less intense and not very organized,
though showers will occur at times, especially in the higher 
terrain directly downwind of the lake. Given the precip will be 
lake-driven by Friday and into the weekend precipitation 
chances will trend to very low values across our Northwest Ohio 
and Central Ohio counties. A few showers may occur across 
Northwest OH on Friday beneath the heart of the trough aloft. 
Some very low precip chances are also in the forecast farther 
west on Saturday, as a shortwave rotating around the backside of
the departing upper trough may bring just enough lift. 

Portions of the area are likely to see their first wintry precip
of the season over the next couple of days. 850mb temperatures
fall to -5 to -7C early Friday through early Saturday, before
